question: Agency Is the Scarce Output
content: Naval argues that intelligence is abundant and agency (the will to act) is scarce. He estimates human output is 99% intelligence and 1% agency, but agency is the bottleneck. AI agents will exercise the agency while humans provide direction.
description: A company has brilliant strategic plans but consistently fails to execute them. Which of Naval's insights best explains this disconnect?
options: The plans are not intelligent enough and need more analysis
The bottleneck is agency — the will to act and execute — not
The company lacks the technology to implement its strategic plans
Market conditions keep changing before plans can be executed
answer: The bottleneck is agency — the will to act and execute — not
explanation: Naval says: 'Human output is 99% intelligence and 1% agency, but agency is the bottleneck. AI agents will exercise the agency while humans provide direction.'

question: Flipping Agency and Intelligence
content: Max Hodak offers a different framing: human output is 70% agency and 30% intelligence. In an AI-powered world, this flips to 30% agency and 70% intelligence because the intelligence part gets outsourced. Agency becomes even more valuable because it's what remains uniquely human.
description: A student worries that AI will make human intelligence obsolete. Based on Max Hodak's framing of the agency-intelligence ratio, what counter-argument would he offer?
options: Human intelligence will always surpass AI in creative domains
When intelligence is abundant from AI, human agency becomes the scarce
AI is not capable of matching human-level intelligence in any domain
The best strategy is to maximize personal intelligence to stay ahead of AI
answer: When intelligence is abundant from AI, human agency becomes the scarce
explanation: Max says: 'I think it's 70% agency and 30% intelligence. And in an AI-powered world that flips to 30% agency, 70% intelligence. Agency gets more valuable.'

question: Vibe Coding Adoption Explosion
content: Naval estimates vibe coding adoption went from 0.01% of the general population to maybe 1% — roughly a 100x increase. He predicts this will grow much further as tools improve and the habit of creating with AI becomes normalized.
description: A reporter claims vibe coding is a niche hobby for programmers and will never reach mainstream adoption. Based on Naval's adoption data, how would you counter this claim?
options: Vibe coding has already seen a roughly 100x increase in adoption from 0.01%
Vibe coding requires programming knowledge so it is inherently limited to developers
Adoption has peaked and is now declining as people lose interest
Only young people use vibe coding so it will grow as the younger generation ages
answer: Vibe coding has already seen a roughly 100x increase in adoption from 0.01%
explanation: Naval says: 'I would estimate vibe coding went from 0.01% to maybe 1% of the general population. A hundred X increase in vibe coding will continue to grow to maybe even 10% of the population.'

question: Gaming Time Replaced by Making
content: Naval predicts that time previously spent consuming media like gaming will shift to making things with AI. When creating becomes as easy as playing a game, people naturally gravitate toward creation rather than passive consumption.
description: A teenager spends 6 hours a day playing video games. According to Naval's prediction about how AI changes behavior, what might happen as vibe coding tools become more accessible and fun?
options: The teenager will still play games since gaming and creating serve different needs
Time previously spent gaming will shift to making things with AI as it becomes as
Gaming will evolve into a creative activity but the time commitment will remain the same
AI will make gaming obsolete entirely as everyone switches to creating
answer: Time previously spent gaming will shift to making things with AI as it becomes as
explanation: Naval says: 'I think people will go from gaming to building things. When creating becomes as easy as playing a game, people gravitate towards creation.'

question: Betting on a Movie From a Book
content: Max Hodak made a bet with Andrej Karpathy that by 2030, the best movie adaptation of a book will be generated by AI, not produced by a traditional Hollywood studio. The bet reflects the belief that long-form video generation will become transformative.
description: A Hollywood executive dismisses AI-generated movies as novelties that will never rival studio productions. Based on Max Hodak's bet with Andrej Karpathy, what timeline does he predict for AI surpassing traditional filmmaking?
options: AI movies will never rival Hollywood because filmmaking is fundamentally a human art
By 2030, the best movie adaptation of a book will be generated by AI, not a studio
AI-generated movies will first dominate animated films before live action by 2040
AI will only be used for special effects and editing, not full movie generation
answer: By 2030, the best movie adaptation of a book will be generated by AI, not a studio
explanation: Max says: 'I made a bet with Andrej Karpathy that by 2030, the best movie adaptation of a book will be generated by AI, not a traditional Hollywood studio.'

question: Multiple Seasons of Lord of the Rings
content: Naval envisions a future where AI generates multiple versions of media — different seasons of Lord of the Rings or The Expanse — exploring different creative directions. The scarcity of human attention becomes the only limit on how much content can be produced.
description: A streaming executive says the bottleneck in producing great shows is finding enough talented writers, directors, and production crews. Based on Naval's vision of AI-generated media, what will the real bottleneck become?
options: Production costs will remain the primary constraint on content creation
Human attention becomes the only limit as AI can produce unlimited variations of
AI will eliminate the need for human creators entirely in the entertainment industry
Copyright law will prevent AI from generating derivative works of existing franchises
answer: Human attention becomes the only limit as AI can produce unlimited variations of
explanation: Naval says: 'We'll have multiple Lord of the Rings, different versions of The Expanse. The scarcity becomes human attention, not creative production.'

question: Art as Conveying Emotion With Intent
content: Naval defines art as intentionally conveying emotion. A sunset is not art (no intent), but a photograph of a sunset that makes someone feel something is art. The key criteria are 1) emotion and 2) intent — the creator must have deliberately aimed to evoke a feeling.
description: A beautiful AI-generated image makes you feel a deep sense of wonder. According to Naval's definition of art, does this image qualify as art?
options: Yes, because it evokes emotion regardless of who or what created it
Only if the human who prompted the AI had the intent to convey that specific
No, because AI is incapable of creating anything that qualifies as art
Only if the image is indistinguishable from something a human artist would create
answer: Only if the human who prompted the AI had the intent to convey that specific
explanation: Naval says: 'Art is conveying emotion with intent.' The key is not just the output but whether the creator deliberately aimed to evoke a feeling.

question: Meaningful Out-of-Distribution Behavior
content: Max Hodak defines something as interesting or creative when it exhibits meaningful out-of-distribution behavior — doing something that isn't just a statistical interpolation of what's been seen before. True novelty means stepping outside the distribution of existing examples.
description: An AI generates a painting that looks exactly like a Monet. Another AI generates a painting that blends Monet's style with architectural blueprints to create something never seen before. According to Max Hodak, which is more creative?
options: The Monet imitation because it perfectly replicates a known artistic style
The blend of Monet and blueprints because it exhibits meaningful
Neither is creative because AI cannot produce creative work by definition
Both are equally creative because creativity is subjective and non-comparable
answer: The blend of Monet and blueprints because it exhibits meaningful
explanation: Max says: 'Interesting or creative means meaningful out-of-distribution behavior — doing something that isn't just a statistical interpolation of what's been seen before.'

question: The Studio Ghibli Pattern Problem
content: The panel discusses the proliferation of Studio Ghibli-style AI images. Naval observes that copying a style is initially fun but quickly becomes boring because it doesn't add anything new. The real value is in creating novel visual languages, not mimicking existing ones.
description: Social media is flooded with AI-generated images in the style of a famous artist. The trend is popular but critics say it adds nothing original. Based on Naval and Max's discussion, what is the fundamental limitation of pure style imitation?
options: Style imitation is legally problematic and could lead to copyright infringement lawsuits
Copying a style is just interpolation within the existing distribution, not meaningful
The style imitation trend is harmless and should be encouraged as artistic expression
Famous artists should release official AI style packs so the results are higher quality
answer: Copying a style is just interpolation within the existing distribution, not meaningful
explanation: Naval says copying a style is initially fun but quickly boring. Max's framework explains why: pure style imitation stays within the existing distribution of examples. The real creative value is novel visual languages.

question: Gödel's Incompleteness and AI Creativity
content: Nivi references Gödel's incompleteness theorems to explore whether AI can have truly new ideas. The theorems show that any formal system has truths that cannot be proven within the system. Naval suggests this implies that true novelty — stepping outside the system — is an inherently human capability.
description: A computer scientist argues that AI can eventually discover everything worth discovering because it can process all existing knowledge. Based on the panel's discussion of Gödel's incompleteness theorems, what is the counter-argument?
options: Gödel's theorems apply only to mathematics, not to creative or scientific discovery
Any formal system has truths outside it, suggesting true novelty requires
AI can overcome Gödel's limitations through brute force computation
Gödel's theorems prove that human creativity is also limited and cannot produce true novelty
answer: Any formal system has truths outside it, suggesting true novelty requires
explanation: The panel discusses whether AI can have truly new ideas. Gödel's theorems suggest that any formal system has unprovable truths. True novelty may require the ability to step outside the current system of knowledge.

question: Generalists Have a Field Day
content: Naval observes that in an AI-powered world, generalists thrive because they can use AI to execute across many domains. The specialist who spent years becoming an expert in one narrow area is now competing with a generalist who can produce expert-level output with AI assistance.
description: A specialist who spent 10 years mastering a single programming language finds their skills less valued. Meanwhile, a generalist with broad knowledge but less depth in any one area is producing more. Based on Naval's observation, what explains this shift?
options: The specialist's language is no longer in demand and they should learn a new one
AI lets generalists produce expert-level output across multiple domains, making
The generalist is probably cutting corners and producing lower quality work
Companies no longer value deep expertise in any domain
answer: AI lets generalists produce expert-level output across multiple domains, making
explanation: Naval says: 'Generalists have a field day because they can use AI to execute across many domains. The specialist who spent years in one narrow area now competes with a generalist producing expert output with AI.'

question: Human Plus AI Versus Pure AI
content: The panel converges on the view that human-plus-AI beats pure AI. The human provides direction, taste, agency, and the ability to step outside the system. AI provides execution, intelligence, and speed. The combination outperforms either alone.
description: Two companies compete: one uses fully autonomous AI for all creative work; the other uses AI as a tool directed by human creatives. Based on the panel's consensus, which approach will produce better results?
options: Pure AI will win because it is faster and costs less than employing humans
Human-plus-AI will win because humans provide direction, taste, and agency that AI
The approaches will produce equivalent results since AI is the main driver in both cases
Humans without AI will outperform both because AI produces generic output
answer: Human-plus-AI will win because humans provide direction, taste, and agency that AI
explanation: The panel converges: 'Human-plus-AI beats pure AI. The human provides direction, taste, agency, and the ability to step outside the system. AI provides intelligence and speed.'
